haiku-low.q1: The unfiltered reports.row_count decides: 10,000 or fewer returns a 200 text/csv response directly. More than 10,000 creates a queued export, returns 202, and emails a 24-hour link.
haiku-low.q2: The insert violates the partial unique index, so the API returns 200 with the existing export's id and status and queues nothing.
haiku-low.q3: The signed download link expires 24 hours after creation. The bucket lifecycle rule deletes the stored file 7 days after creation.
haiku-low.q4: Three attempts, with retries after 60 s and 300 s. After the last failure the row is marked failed, and the user gets a report_export_failed email.
haiku-low.q5: Both the direct and background export paths read report rows only from the read replica.
haiku-low.q6: Status is stored in the report_exports table in the primary database. The page keeps no state: it calls GET .../exports/latest on load and polls GET /api/exports/{export_id} every 5 seconds.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000 rows at a time from the replica, encodes them to CSV, and uploads 8 MB multipart parts, so memory holds only one batch and one buffer.
haiku-low.q8: Any exception triggers abort_multipart. A crash or timeout leaves an invisible incomplete upload discarded within 24 hours. The next attempt starts over from the first row with a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: They are saved as the filters and columns fields on the report_exports row at creation. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job loads the row from the primary database.
haiku-low.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running enforces it; the losing insert gets the existing export back.
haiku-low.q11: object_key must be saved, meaning the file is complete, before the link email is sent. If the row is already succeeded or failed, the job does nothing; if running with object_key set, it goes straight to sending the email.
haiku-low.q12: If the replica fails mid-stream, the API drops the connection. The page saves no file, shows the failure message, and nothing retries automatically.

sonnet.q1: The unfiltered reports.row_count decides. 10,000 rows or fewer: the CSV is returned directly in the same response (200, text/csv), with no job and nothing stored. More than 10,000: the API saves an export record, queues a background job and returns 202 (id, status queued). The job writes the file to the exports bucket and emails the user a link valid for 24 hours.
sonnet.q2: The insert violates the partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued/running. The API returns 200 with the existing export's id and status, and queues nothing.
sonnet.q3: The signed link works 24 hours. The file is removed by the bucket's lifecycle rule 7 days after creation (no cleanup job).
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts (retries wait 60 s, then 300 s). After attempt 3 fails, on_final_failure sets status failed (with error and finished_at), then sends a report_export_failed email. The page shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.' and the user can click again to start a new export. If the failure email fails, it is only logged; the page still shows failed.
sonnet.q5: The read replica (both small and large paths). Export records live in the primary database.
sonnet.q6: In the status column of the report_exports row in the primary database. The page polls GET /api/exports/{export_id} every 5 seconds while queued or running, stopping at succeeded or failed. On reopening, it calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest to get the user's newest export, then polls if still active. The page keeps no export state of its own.
sonnet.q7: It streams in parts rather than loading everything. It reads 5,000 rows at a time from the replica, encodes them to CSV in an in-memory buffer, and uploads each time the buffer reaches 8 MB via multipart upload. Memory holds at most one batch plus one 8 MB buffer. About 115 parts, well under the 10,000-part limit. (The document does not state the 512 MB figure itself.)
sonnet.q8: On an exception, the job calls abort_multipart and re-raises. If the worker crashes or times out (30 min), the upload is never completed, so nothing becomes visible and the bucket discards it after 24 h. The next attempt starts again at step 6 and begins a new upload from the first row; nothing carries over. If complete_multipart succeeded but saving object_key failed, the next attempt rewrites the file and complete_multipart replaces it.
sonnet.q9: They are frozen on the report_exports row (filters and columns columns) in the primary database. The job payload carries only the export_id, and the job loads the row to get them.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status in ('queued','running') in the primary database, created by the migration in step 1. The second insert violates it.
sonnet.q11: The file must be complete: complete_multipart succeeded and object_key is saved on the row. If rerun when the row is succeeded or failed, the job returns and does nothing. If the row is running with object_key set, it skips writing and goes straight to step 8 (sign the URL and send the email, then mark succeeded).
sonnet.q12: If the replica fails before any bytes are sent, the API returns 503. If it fails mid-stream, the API drops the connection. Either way the page saves no file and shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.' Nothing retries automatically.
